title: A multi-objective model for a nurse scheduling problem by emphasizing human factors.
problem: Assigning nurses to departments and shifts based on human factors (skill, preference, compatibility) to enhance teamwork and healthcare efficiency.
contribution: A unique multi-objective mathematical model for nurse scheduling is proposed, considering nurses' decision-making styles.
method: Three meta-heuristics (multi-objective Keshtel algorithm, NSGA-II, and multi-objective tabu search) and data envelopment analysis for ranking Pareto solutions are developed.
data_setup: A real-life case at a large hospital in Tehran, Iran.
results: The applicability and effectiveness of the proposed model are assessed based on experimental results.
